title: Your rights as a consumer
examples: What do I do if I buy something online and it doesn't arrive?
How long do I have to keep a receipt for a return?
Is a warranty the same as a guarantee?

explain.say: Today we learn about your rights when you buy things.
If something you buy is faulty, you have specific rights.
A warranty is a promise about how long something will work.
If you want a refund, you usually need proof of purchase.
If the item is faulty, you should tell the seller quickly.

items: What: Report the fault to the store

explain.say: In real life, if your phone charger stops working, you use these rights.

faq.q: What is the difference between a warranty and a guarantee?
faq.a: A warranty is often a promise from the maker. A guarantee is usually a promise from the seller.

faq.q: Do I always get a full refund if something is faulty?
faq.a: Depending on the fault, you might get a repair, a replacement, or a refund.
asks: Can I choose what I get?

faq.q: How long do I have to return something I don't like?
faq.a: Some shops have a 'change of mind' policy, but this is different from a faulty item.
asks: Does the store have a return window?

faq.q: What if I lose my receipt?
faq.a: Some stores might accept proof of purchase using a bank statement or card record.
asks: Do I need the original receipt?

faq.q: Can I return something if I used it once?
faq.a: If the fault was there from the start, you can usually return it. If you broke it, that is different.

facts: Faulty goods mean the item did not work correctly when you bought it.
A warranty is a written promise about product performance.
Always keep your proof of purchase, like a receipt or bank slip.
Your rights are designed to keep you safe as a buyer.

quiz.say: You buy a toaster, and after one week, the lever does not pop up.

options.show: You should just buy a new toaster.
options.say: You should just buy a new toaster.

options.show: You must wait six months to complain.
options.say: You must wait six months to complain.

options.show: You can only get a refund if you bring the box.
options.say: You can only get a refund if you bring the box.

options.show: You should ask the store for a replacement.
options.say: You should ask the store for a replacement.

quiz.why: Because the item is faulty, you have the right to a fix or a swap.

wrong.0: This ignores your existing rights with the seller.
wrong.1: Faulty goods rights are usually much quicker to claim.
wrong.2: The fault is the main issue, not the packaging.

quiz.say: A seller promises the washing machine will work for three years.

options.show: You must check the law book for this.
options.say: You must check the law book for this.

options.show: This promise is likely a warranty.
options.say: This promise is likely a warranty.

quiz.why: A warranty is a specific promise about how long something should function.

wrong.0: A specific time period suggests a formal promise.
wrong.1: The promise itself is the key piece of information here.
wrong.3: Guarantee usually comes from the person you paid.

quiz.say: You bought shoes last month, and the sole started peeling off.

options.show: You should take the shoes and your receipt back.
options.say: You should take the shoes and your receipt back.

options.show: You should post a photo online.
options.say: You should post a photo online.

options.show: You can wait until next month to return them.
options.say: You can wait until next month to return them.

options.show: You should just buy a pair of different shoes.
options.say: You should just buy a pair of different shoes.

quiz.why: You need the proof of purchase and the faulty item together.

wrong.1: While useful, the store needs the physical item.
wrong.2: The sooner you report a fault, the better your case.
wrong.3: This ignores the fact that the original pair is faulty.
